key_insight: A PINN gives the most accurate point-wise solution for this Couette flow problem, while a data-trained DeepONet is far faster and generalizes well across slip and wall-velocity conditions.
engineering_relevance: The work points to a practical surrogate modeling path for real-time prediction and rapid parametric sweeps in wall-bounded fluid mechanics with dynamic slip.
method: PINN solves the governing equations for a fixed physical setup using physics constraints.
DeepONet is trained on high-fidelity Crank-Nicolson data to learn the solution operator.
The model is evaluated on unseen and out-of-distribution slip/velocity cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a PINN relative L2 error of 0.083%, DeepONet mean relative errors of 0.36% on unseen data and 0.88% OOD, and about 540X speedup over the numerical solver.
watch_item: DeepONet is highly efficient, but it depends on quality training data and may need retraining or augmentation when the operating regime changes beyond the sampled parameter space.
paper_title: Solution of the Newtonian plane Couette flow with dynamic wall slip using machine-learning methods
